reports.title: Universal Technical Institute Reports Fiscal Year 2026 Fourth Quarter and Year-End Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2027 Financial Outlook
section: “Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, we expect revenue between $925 million and $945 million, while new student starts are expected to grow 9% at the midpoint,” continued Schuman. Our baseline adjusted EBITDA, excluding planned growth investments, is expected to be between $135 million and $141 million, while reported adjusted EBITDA is expected to be between $100 million and $106 million, inclusive of approximately $35 million of EBITDA impact due to growth investments in four planned new campus openings, new program launches and skilled trades capacity expansions, subject to required regulatory approvals. We view these as disciplined, high-return investments that will temporarily pressure margins while building meaningful earnings power for the years ahead. We will see these returns start to materialize in fiscal 2028, when we expect revenue of more than $1 billion and adjusted EBITDA approaching $150 million, and in fiscal 2029, we expect to surpass $1.2 billion in annual revenue with adjusted EBITDA approaching $220 million.”

desk.headline: Revenue up 6% to $235.9m, slight beat; EPS 32c just short; first FY27 outlook points to near-zero profit as campus build-out peaks
results: Quarterly sales rose 6% to $235.9m; diluted EPS slipped to 32c from 34c as costs for new campuses and programs rose.
Both divisions grew: UTI (transport and skilled trades) revenue rose 6% to $153.6m and Concorde (healthcare) 6% to $82.2m.

Full-year revenue of $897.0m, net income of $33.6m (down 47%) and adjusted EBITDA of $102.0m all landed inside the ranges cut in August; full-year starts of 31,873 came in just under the 31,900–32,300 range.
Heavy building pushed spending on property and equipment to $106.4m from $42.0m, so adjusted free cash flow turned negative at -$12.6m.
Year-end liquidity was $320.8m against total debt of $114.3m, including $50m drawn on the credit line; three new campuses opened during the year.

guidance.summary: First fiscal 2027 outlook: revenue of $925–945m and starts up about 9%, but net income of only $0–5m as about $35m of growth spending on four new campuses and 15+ programs hits earnings. Longer-term targets of more than $1.2bn revenue and adjusted EBITDA near $220m in fiscal 2029 were reaffirmed.

points: Management says demand for skilled trades is strong and that capacity, "not student interest," is what holds growth back in several markets.

The soft fourth-quarter starts were blamed on high-school admissions staffing and training at a few auto and diesel campuses; reps were raised to over 185 from about 155, with the full benefit only expected by Q4 FY27.
The CFO said the weaker starts mean fewer students carried into fiscal 2027, which slows near-term revenue growth, and called this temporary.
A shift towards shorter skilled-trades programmes will squeeze margins; the larger Skilled Trades Max campus model and modest price rises in welding, HVAC, electrical and aviation are meant to help.
The company says it can fund the rest of the build-out without new financing; over 70% of FY27 capex is for growth.
